Definition: from G5465; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):--bit, bridle.
BiblicalUsage: Chalinos is a bit, a bridle. James says we put bits in the horses' mouths to turn about their whole body, and John sees blood come out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bit is small and the body is large, and that is the whole of James's point — and the winepress is the warning of what happens when no one holds the reins.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
